chunks.content: # Realistic Piercing Creation Tutorial in CLO This document explains the detailed process of creating a realistic window ring (piercing) on clothing using CLO software. It covers the replacement concept, 3D positioning, sewing techniques, simulation adjustments, and troubleshooting for natural fit and stability. --- ## Inserting and Positioning the Ring Object This section covers how to insert a ring object in CLO and position it accurately using virtual models and coordinate adjustments for realistic collision and placement. - Insert the completed ring object into the 3D workspace. - Set the ring as an "added option" and assign it a virtual model for real collision detection. - The ring's position can be viewed on different floors/windows in the 3D window. - Use the replacement concept to avoid simulation instability by not wearing the ring directly on the garment mesh. - The replacement concept involves sewing the ring to a round piece of fabric of nearly the same size, which acts as an intermediary. - Create a round board piece by drawing a circle matching the ring's diameter (e.g., 53 mm). - The placement shadow depends on the board's position in the 3D window; the board is centered on the ground plane's crosshair. - Hide the virtual model temporarily to focus on the ground plane and ensure the ring is positioned centrally. - Adjust the board piece's size to be slightly smaller to facilitate wrapping around the ring. - Use world coordinates and multiple viewing angles (including side views) to align the ring and fabric piece naturally and parallel to the garment surface. --- ## Preparing the Board Piece and Sewing Setup This section details how to prepare the fabric board piece, freeze it to avoid unwanted simulation effects, and sew it properly for the ring replacement. - The fabric thickness is pre-set to 2 mm; this may make the board piece appear thick. - Sew the board piece to the garment but do not simulate immediately. - Freeze the board piece’s transformations to stabilize it before running simulations. - After freezing, simulate the garment to see the board piece’s interaction. - Use the quick arrangement tool to position the circle exactly over the board piece. - Slightly shrink the board piece around its center to allow it to wrap tightly around the ring. - Place the circle back into the virtual model to avoid affecting simulation directly. - Activate the board piece’s cross center to control its shrinkage symmetrically. - Run simulation to check the overlap and wrapping of the board piece around the ring. --- ## Sewing and Adjusting Double-Layer Board Pieces This section explains how to sew a double-layer fabric board piece around the ring, manage sewing lines, and ensure proper alignment for natural appearance. - Prepare a double-layer board piece and add the circular ring shape to it. - Simulate and adjust sewing lines carefully. - Delete any initial sewing lines that do not align properly.

chunks.content: - Run simulation to check the overlap and wrapping of the board piece around the ring. --- ## Sewing and Adjusting Double-Layer Board Pieces This section explains how to sew a double-layer fabric board piece around the ring, manage sewing lines, and ensure proper alignment for natural appearance. - Prepare a double-layer board piece and add the circular ring shape to it. - Simulate and adjust sewing lines carefully. - Delete any initial sewing lines that do not align properly. - Sew the piece in sections, aligning the sewing points to the outside edges of the board piece. - Use fold sewing techniques by sewing the inside first, followed by the bottom. - After sewing, simulate to check the board piece's interaction with the ring and garment. --- ## Final Positioning and Simulation Optimization This section covers the fine-tuning of the ring's position, simulation stability improvements, and resolving penetration issues. - Activate the circle and virtual model; adjust their layering using the grid tool. - Use the 3D window’s positioning ball to pull and adjust the ring in all axes. - Hide the model temporarily to adjust the back frame and ensure symmetrical positioning. - For simulation stability, reduce particle diameter settings: - Set the particle diameter of the two board pieces to 5. - Set the circle’s surface diameter to 0. - Adjust collision thickness parameters for the board pieces. - Simulate and observe if the ring is naturally worn on the garment. - If penetration occurs, reduce board piece particle diameter further (down to 3) to resolve overlaps. - Delete the circle object after it has served its purpose and simulate again. - The ring should now be realistically wrapped and positioned on the garment. --- ## Final Adjustments and Seam Allowance Management This section discusses final fit adjustments and seam allowance optimization to achieve a realistic ring appearance. - Sew the final points around the ring carefully. - Note that the ring position may be slightly raised, causing an arch; use the positioning ball during simulation to adjust height gradually. - Achieve a natural curve and fit by small iterative adjustments. - In some cases, the ring can be made from a single-layer board piece folded over rather than a double-layer. - Cut unnecessary seam allowances away and re-add only the required allowances. - Simulate again to confirm the final realistic ring fit and finish. --- # Summary This tutorial guides through creating a realistic piercing ring on clothing in CLO using a replacement fabric piece method. It emphasizes precise 3D positioning, sewing techniques, simulation stability enhancements, and final fit adjustments to ensure the ring integrates naturally and realistically with the garment.
